items.title: Interactive SVG to TTF Font Mapper
items.basis: Local SVG import, keyboard assignment, TTF export
items.prompt: User uploads an SVG file. A visual keyboard interface appears, allowing the user to drag and drop glyphs onto specific keys. A live preview window shows how text typed with the assigned keys will appear. Controls for fine-tuning glyph position, scale, and rotation per key are available. User can save the project state. Upon clicking 'Export TTF', a high-fidelity TrueType font is generated locally, preserving intricate details via a 4096-unit grid. Acceptance criteria: Font exports correctly, glyphs map as assigned, live preview is accurate, project saves and loads. Runtime design: Optimize SVG parsing for immediate display, use WebGL for live preview rendering, lazy-load font generation.
items.why_weird: The core mechanism is the direct, local translation of visual arbitrary vector art into a structured typographic system, treating the keyboard as a canvas for digital ornamentation, rather than just symbolic representation.

items.title: AI Contact Sheet Auto-Vectorizer and Fontifier
items.basis: Raster image import (PNG, JPG, WebP), browser-based tracing, automatic glyph assignment
items.prompt: User drops a 3x3 grid of 9 distinct ornaments (e.g., from an AI image generator) into 'THE PILE'. The app defaults to '3x3' / '5 colors' / 'Detailed' / 'Normal white removal'. It automatically traces each distinct color region into SVG paths within the browser. Nine full-color vector assets are created and assigned to available keyboard keys. The user can then export these as individual SVGs or as a single monochrome TTF font. Acceptance criteria: Each of the 9 ornaments is successfully traced into vector paths, assigned to a key, and exported as a functional TTF. Runtime design: Employ a multi-threaded Web Worker for raster tracing to prevent UI freezes, use efficient canvas rendering for previews.
items.why_weird: This process re-imagines AI-generated 'contact sheets' not as final outputs, but as raw material for a local, analog-like font fabrication pipeline, where the machine learning output is deconstructed and reformed into functional typographic units.

items.title: Color SVG Sheet Harvester with Auto-Key Fill
items.basis: Single SVG import (sheet layout), gutter detection, automatic glyph assignment
items.prompt: User imports a single SVG file containing multiple, separated symbols arranged in a grid. The 'Sheet Harvester' visually analyzes the white space (gutters) to identify individual glyph boundaries. The user can select specific regions or use 'HARVEST ALL + FILL KEYS' to import all detected designs and automatically assign them to the next available keyboard keys. An option to disable auto-fill allows manual assignment. Acceptance criteria: Glyphs are accurately segmented, imported into the pile, and assigned to keys as requested, with automatic assignment prioritizing standard keyboard layouts. Runtime design: Utilize image processing algorithms on a temporary canvas rendering for gutter detection, manage glyph data in memory efficiently.
items.why_weird: It treats a composite SVG as a literal sheet of 'stamps' or 'seals' that can be automatically 'cut out' and assigned to functional keyboard inputs, mirroring a physical process of die-cutting and distribution.

items.title: Local Raster Tracing Engine for Flat-Color Art
items.basis: Browser-based raster tracing (PNG, JPG, WebP, SVG), adjustable white removal threshold, color preservation
items.prompt: User uploads a raster image (PNG, JPG, WebP) or an existing SVG intended for tracing. The 'COLOR VECTOR FOUNDRY' allows selection of tracing detail ('Compact', 'Detailed', 'Maximum detail') and color handling ('3-8 colors'). A slider adjusts the 'white removal threshold' to handle off-white backgrounds. The engine traces color regions into SVG paths locally. Acceptance criteria: Traced SVGs accurately represent the flat-color regions of the input image, with adjustable parameters yielding predictable variations. Runtime design: Implement edge detection and region-filling algorithms in Web Workers, use precise color quantization for dominant color identification.
items.why_weird: This feature democratizes vectorization by performing complex image processing (raster-to-vector conversion) client-side, transforming flat-color raster art into usable vector paths without external services, framed as a 'foundry' for digitized ornamentation.

items.title: High-Precision TTF Export with 4096-Unit Grid
items.basis: TTF export with increased coordinate precision
items.prompt: User has an editable project or original SVGs. They initiate a new TTF export. The application utilizes a 4096-unit grid for outline generation, significantly higher than standard methods. The user is prompted to provide a new family name for the regenerated font to avoid conflicts. Acceptance criteria: Exported TTF files contain outlines with increased coordinate precision, leading to visibly smoother curves and sharper details for small features, compared to lower-precision exports. Runtime design: Map Bézier curve control points to the higher-resolution grid during the TTF generation phase.
items.why_weird: The emphasis on a vastly increased unit grid for font export transforms the technical aspect of typography into a pursuit of micro-level aesthetic fidelity, akin to enhancing the resolution of a digital sculpture.

items.title: Vector Glyph Optimization for Font Conversion
items.basis: SVG optimization for point limits and file size
items.prompt: User imports SVGs that may be overly complex for font conversion. The system attempts to optimize these individual SVG files, aiming to reduce their size (e.g., below 2MB) by removing non-essential metadata and reducing coordinate decimal precision where beneficial, without deleting anchor points. This optimization is a 'best effort' to ensure compatibility with font conversion. Acceptance criteria: Optimized SVGs are demonstrably smaller and/or have fewer points while retaining visual integrity and suitability for TTF export. Runtime design: Implement a series of SVG simplification algorithms, prioritize path data cleanup.
items.why_weird: This prompt frames optimization not as a technical necessity, but as a form of 'sculptural reduction' applied to digital vector forms, honing them down to their essential structure for typographic reincarnation.

items.title: Full-Color SVG Extraction from Composite Sheets
items.basis: Individual multicolor SVG export from traced or raw SVG sheets
items.prompt: User selects a traced design or an original SVG from 'THE PILE'. They choose to export it as an individual, full-color SVG using the 'Sheet Harvester' options. Settings include 'Preserve original colors', 'Auto' (aiming for <2MB), 'Maximum fidelity', or 'Compact (3 decimals)'. The system detects bright colors and attempts to separate compound paths. Acceptance criteria: Exported individual SVGs accurately represent the selected design with its original colors and structure, meeting size targets where applicable. Runtime design: Utilize color-aware path separation logic and adaptive precision reduction.
items.why_weird: This feature treats each symbol on a sheet not just as a shape, but as an independent artifact capable of carrying its own color palette, allowing for the export of 'miniature stained-glass windows' from a larger composition.

items.title: Custom Box and Manual Design Import for Sheet Harvester
items.basis: Manual region definition for glyph extraction
items.prompt: When automatic gutter detection fails or the layout is irregular, the user can employ 'Draw a custom box' within the 'Sheet Harvester' preview. After drawing a bounding box around a missed design, they can add it as a new glyph. Alternatively, the 'Import whole SVG as ONE icon' option bypasses slicing entirely. Acceptance criteria: User-defined boxes accurately capture desired glyph areas, and manual imports correctly represent the selected or whole SVG as a single glyph. Runtime design: Implement interactive canvas drawing tools for bounding box creation.
items.why_weird: This prompt introduces a tactile, 'manual drafting' element to the automated harvesting process, allowing users to physically 'cut out' or 'frame' desired components from digital compositions, reclaiming control through direct intervention.

items.title: SVG to Font Outline Point Limit Handling
items.basis: Identifying and managing SVGs unsuitable for font conversion due to complexity
items.prompt: The system identifies SVGs that are too complex (e.g., exceeding memory limits or having excessively dense paths) for direct conversion into font outlines. These are marked as 'SVG ONLY'. The user is informed and can still export these as standalone SVGs but cannot assign them to font keys. Acceptance criteria: Complex SVGs are correctly flagged as 'SVG ONLY', preventing assignment to font keys, while still being available for separate SVG export. Runtime design: Implement real-time complexity analysis during SVG import and processing.
items.why_weird: This feature creates a classification system for digital assets, distinguishing between those suitable for typographic embodiment and those that remain 'pure vector artworks,' acknowledging inherent limitations in translation and functional purpose.

items.title: Interactive Project Saving and LocalStorage Autosave
items.prompt: User works on importing SVGs, assigning keys, and adjusting parameters. They can manually 'Save project' to store the current state (keyboard mappings, imported assets, settings) in a JSON file locally. The browser's localStorage also provides an autosave function, periodically storing the project state to prevent data loss. Acceptance criteria: Projects can be manually saved and reliably reloaded. Autosave prevents significant data loss during unintended session closures. Runtime design: Serialize project state into JSON, manage localStorage quota efficiently, provide clear user feedback on save status.
items.why_weird: This prompt highlights the 'local-first' nature of the application, framing project saving not just as data persistence but as the creation of a personal, self-contained 'digital artifact' that can be revisited and modified, emphasizing user agency over cloud reliance.
